summary:
We developed NASA Earth System Trend Detector, an interactive client-server web platform that transforms complex satellite climate archives into instant, actionable meteorological analytics. Powered by the NASA POWER Temporal Daily API, our solution allows users to query historical temperature (T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN) and precipitation (PRECTOTCORR) data for any GPS coordinates worldwide or preset global benchmarks in under two seconds.

Our decoupled Python architecture (FastAPI asynchronous backend and Streamlit frontend) directly addresses the technical barrier of working with raw space datasets. It automatically cleans missing satellite flags (-999), processes time series using Pandas, calculates statistical extremes and net climate trends, and generates interactive charts.

This tool is vital because it democratizes access to open NASA Earth observation data, empowering farmers, renewable energy planners, educators, and researchers to make informed climate decisions without requiring coding skills or costly local weather stations.
details:
What it does & How it works: A client-server web application (FastAPI + Streamlit) that automatically requests, cleans, and visualizes climate and weather data from the NASA POWER API for chosen coordinates and timeframes.

Маркер Benefits & Impact: Provides fast, simplified access to reliable meteorological trends without complex software, making initial climate analysis accessible to a wide audience.

Маркер Technologies used: Python, FastAPI, Streamlit, httpx, and Pandas.

Маркер Creativity & Factors: Combines a powerful space agency API with a clean, intuitive interface. The team ensured data reliability by filtering out anomalous or missing records and implemented quick-access location presets for user convenience.
